review_candidates.title: Business System Analyst
review_candidates.description: Business Analyst Employment Type Full-Time Job Purpose The Business Analyst is responsible for bridging the gap between business needs and technology solutions. The role involves gathering, analyzing, documenting, and managing business and system requirements throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). The Business Analyst works closely with clients, business stakeholders, Product Owners, Project Managers, UI/UX Designers, Developers, QA Engineers, and other technical teams to ensure that requirements are clearly understood, properly documented, technically feasible, and successfully translated into high-quality software solutions. Key Responsibilities 1. Business & Requirements Analysis Gather and analyze business requirements from clients, users, and stakeholders through meetings, interviews, workshops, and document analysis. Understand business objectives, operational processes, customer needs, problems, and improvement opportunities. Analyze existing processes and systems and identify gaps, inefficiencies, risks, and areas for improvement. Define and document As-Is and To-Be processes. Conduct Gap Analysis and Impact Analysis. Translate business needs into clear, structured, and actionable functional requirements. Identify functional and non-functional requirements. Define business rules, validations, workflows, user roles, permissions, and expected system behavior. Ensure requirements are complete, consistent, measurable, feasible, and testable. Identify assumptions, dependencies, constraints, and risks related to requirements. 2. Requirements Documentation Prepare and maintain professional requirements documentation. Develop Business Requirements Documents (BRD), Functional Requirements Documents (FRD), and/or Software Requirements Specifications (SRS) as required. Create detailed User Stories and clear Acceptance Criteria. Prepare Use Cases, business scenarios, process flows, and workflow diagrams. Document business rules, data requirements, system behavior, and integration requirements. Maintain requirements traceability throughout the project lifecycle. Keep all documentation updated following approved changes. 3. User Stories & Product Backlog Convert business requirements into clear and actionable User Stories. Define acceptance criteria covering functional and business scenarios. Identify dependencies and relationships between requirements. Work with Product Owners and Product Managers to refine, prioritize, and maintain the Product Backlog. Participate in Backlog Refinement and ensure User Stories are sufficiently detailed before development. Clarify requirements and business rules for Development and QA teams. Review completed features against approved requirements and acceptance criteria. Support prioritization of features based on business value, customer needs, and project priorities. 4. Agile & Scrum Participate in Agile/Scrum ceremonies including: Sprint Planning Daily Stand-ups Backlog Refinement Sprint Review Sprint Retrospective Provide business and functional clarification throughout development. Support the Scrum Master and Product Owner in maintaining an organized and actionable backlog. Identify and escalate requirement-related blockers. Contribute to continuous improvement of the product development and requirements management process. 5. Business Process Analysis Analyze and document business workflows and operational procedures. Identify bottlenecks, duplicated activities, manual processes, and inefficiencies. Design optimized To-Be processes aligned with business objectives. Create process maps and workflow diagrams using appropriate tools and methodologies such as BPMN. Assess the impact of proposed software solutions on existing business processes. 6. Software & System Analysis Analyze software requirements from both business and functional perspectives. Develop a strong understanding of system functionality and major software components. Understand system integrations, data flows, APIs, and dependencies at a functional level. Define integration requirements, data inputs/outputs, validations, and expected behavior. Understand basic database concepts and data relationships. Use SQL when required for data validation, investigation, and analysis. Collaborate with Developers, Technical Leads, and Architects to clarify functional requirements. Ensure business requirements are technically understandable and aligned with the proposed solution. 7. UI/UX Collaboration Work closely with UI/UX Designers to translate business requirements into effective user experiences. Review wireframes, prototypes, user journeys, and designs against business requirements. Ensure all required user actions, scenarios, validations, and business rules are reflected in the design. Provide functional clarification to UI/UX teams. Identify missing or unclear scenarios before development. 8. Quality Assurance & UAT Work closely with QA Engineers throughout the testing lifecycle. Ensure requirements and Acceptance Criteria provide sufficient information for test-case development. Review test scenarios against approved requirements. Support QA teams in understanding expected system behavior. Analyze requirement-related defects and clarify whether issues are defects, requirement gaps, or change requests. Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Coordinate with business stakeholders during UAT. Review UAT feedback and coordinate required changes with relevant teams. Verify that delivered functionality meets approved requirements. 9. Client & Stakeholder Management Act as a communication bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams. Conduct requirements workshops and discovery sessions with clients. Understand and manage stakeholder expectations. Communicate complex technical concepts in clear business language. Resolve requirement conflicts, gaps, and ambiguities through structured analysis and stakeholder discussions. Obtain clarification, confirmation, and approval of requirements when required. Maintain effective professional relationships with clients and internal stakeholders. 10. Change & Scope Management Identify, document, and assess changes to approved requirements. Perform impact analysis on scope, timeline, resources, cost, functionality, and dependencies. Coordinate Change Requests with Product, Project Management, and technical teams. Identify and escalate unauthorized scope changes. Maintain records of approved and rejected changes. Update User Stories and related documentation following approved changes. 11. Data Analysis & Reporting Analyze business and operational data to support decision-making. Identify trends, issues, anomalies, and improvement opportunities. Define requirements for reports, dashboards, KPIs, and business metrics. Validate system reports against approved business requirements. Work with technical teams to clarify reporting logic and calculations. Use Excel, SQL, or other analytical tools when required. 12. Documentation & Knowledge Management Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation, including: BRD / FRD / SRS User Stories Acceptance Criteria Use Cases Business Rules Process Flows Data Requirements UAT Documentation Change Requests Requirements Traceability Ensure that documentation accurately reflects the current product and is accessible to relevant stakeholders. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Engineering, MIS, or a related field. 3–5 years of proven experience as a Business Analyst, preferably within a software development company, technology company, SaaS environment, or digital transformation project. Strong experience in software requirements gathering, analysis, and documentation. Practical experience working with Agile/Scrum development teams. Experience working directly with Developers, QA Engineers, Product Owners, and business stakeholders. Client-facing requirements-gathering experience is highly preferred. Technical Skills Business Analysis Requirements Gathering & Analysis Business Process Analysis Gap Analysis Root Cause Analysis Impact Analysis As-Is / To-Be Analysis Business Rules Process Optimization Stakeholder Analysis Requirements Engineering Functional & Non-Functional Requirements User Stories Acceptance Criteria Use Cases Requirements Traceability Requirements Prioritization Change Management Agile & Product Agile Methodologies Scrum Product Backlog Sprint Planning Backlog Refinement MVP Concepts Product Requirements Software & Technical Knowledge SDLC Web & Mobile Applications Basic Software Architecture Understanding APIs & System Integrations Data Flow Database Concepts Basic to Intermediate SQL Functional Testing & UAT Modeling & Documentation BPMN UML Use Case Diagrams Activity Diagrams Process Flow Diagrams User Flows Wireframes Tools Experience with the following tools is preferred: Jira Confluence Microsoft Excel Microsoft Word Microsoft Visio Draw.io Lucidchart Figma Postman SQL Tools Soft Skills Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong attention to detail. Excellent documentation and presentation skills. Strong stakeholder management capabilities. Ability to understand complex business problems and translate them into software requirements. Strong negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. Excellent organization and time-management skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities. Proactive, structured, and solution-oriented mindset. Ability to work independently and within cross-functional teams. Strong customer and business-oriented approach. Ability to work effectively under pressure and meet deadlines. Preferred Certifications The following certifications are considered an advantage: IIBA – ECBA / CCBA / CBAP PMI-PBA Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO) Other recognized Business Analysis, Agile, or Product Management certifications.
